question:
A student argues:

"Since free electrons in a metal move randomly with very high speeds, some electrons should naturally fly out of the metal into vacuum even without supplying any external energy."

Critically evaluate this claim and decide whether it is correct or incorrect.

Your evaluation must clearly identify the physical origin of the **surface barrier** at the metal–vacuum interface that prevents spontaneous escape of electrons.

options.A: The claim is correct because gravitational attraction of the heavy metal lattice is too weak to stop fast electrons from escaping
options.B: The claim is correct because electrons are prevented from escaping only by collisions with gas molecules outside the metal
options.C: The claim is incorrect because when an electron tries to leave, the surface region becomes positively charged and electrostatic attraction pulls the electron back, creating a surface barrier
options.D: The claim is incorrect because the strong nuclear force at the surface binds free electrons to the outermost layer
